title: The Word's tabernacle and the body's willing death
english: For the tabernacle of the Word and God is not the same thing as the Word himself, and it was through this tabernacle that the blessed Stephen beheld the divine glory. Before the passion, Christ repeatedly foretold his bodily death, saying that he would be handed over to those around the high priests, and proclaiming the trophy of the cross. After the passion, having risen on the third day from the dead, when his disciples doubted that he had been raised, he appeared to them in that very body, acknowledged that he had all his flesh together with his bones, and placing before their eyes his wounded sides, showed them the prints of the nails. But their impious slander can be refuted in just a few words. First of all, if he had not willingly handed over his own body to the slaughter of death for the salvation of human beings, they would be attributing great weakness to him, because he was not able to hold back the assault of his enemies.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is arguing against the Arians that Christ had a real human body, and here he contrasts the tabernacle of the Word with the body's willing surrender to death.

title: Why the Arians deny Christ a soul
english: Why, then, do they make so much of showing that Christ took up a soulless body, fabricating earthy deceits? So that if they are able to corrupt some people and get them to define the matter this way, they may then attach the alterations of the passions to the Spirit and easily persuade them that the changeable was not begotten from the unchangeable nature. Jeremiah, speaking in agreement with these things, introduces the voices of God which he serves, and through them shows that God does not accept even the intercessions of the righteous, if they should choose to plead on behalf of murderers. And the Lord said to me, saying, “If Moses and Samuel stood before my face, my soul is not toward them” (Jeremiah 15:1).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is refuting the Arian claim that Christ took a soulless body, and here he explains their motive and then cites Jeremiah's words about God rejecting intercession for murderers.

title: Christ's soul led the thief's soul into paradise
english: But if through the appearing of Christ the human race is being brought into paradise, and if at the hour he was crucified he foretold that he would bring the thief there that very day while his body still lay cast into the tomb, then it is established that the soul of Christ, dwelling together properly with the Word and God who encompasses all created things at once, brought the kindred soul of the man into paradise. For it is nowhere written that before the resurrection of the holy body the thief's body went ahead and received the promise. It follows, then, to think sensibly that the soul, kindly guiding the kindred soul, since it indeed possessed the greater authority, was bringing the promise to fulfillment that very day, and was leading it into the special inheritance, opening paradise.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that Christ possessed a real human soul, now using the promise to the thief on the cross as proof that Christ's soul, united to the Word, entered paradise while his body still lay in the tomb.
